note: Ingestion and normalisation rules. These are policy, not inference — every one was decided by the client and is applied uniformly across the corpus. Anything the rules cannot settle is surfaced on the dashboard rather than guessed at silently.

speaker_resolution.detail: Fathom tags the closer with a '(Primal Instinct)' suffix on their speaker label. That label identifies the rep. Every other speaker label in the transcript collapses to a single 'prospect' role.
handles: Diarization swapping speakers on short turns — role is assigned per label, not per line, so a swap misattributes a line but never invents a third participant
A prospect changing device mid-call and acquiring a new label (e.g. 'Francisco Adain Vega' becoming "Paco's iPhone 17") — both labels collapse to the same prospect role
speaker_resolution.known_limit: Because diarization genuinely swaps lines, per-line attribution stays approximate. Talk-ratio and who-raised-the-objection metrics are therefore NOT published. Role-level facts (an objection occurred, a phase was run) are safe; line-level ones are not.
speaker_resolution.multi_rep_calls: If more than one '(Primal Instinct)' label appears, the rep with the most speaking turns is the closer; the rest are logged as additional_reps.

prospect_identity.detail: Prospect name is taken from the file title where present ('Name x Rep'). For untitled files ('Impromptu Zoom Meeting') it is recovered from the first non-rep speaker label in the transcript.
prospect_identity.normalisation: Lowercased, punctuation and device suffixes stripped, whitespace collapsed. Used as the deal key.

deal_merging.detail: Multiple calls with the same canonical prospect are a single deal. The deal carries the outcome of its LAST call chronologically, since that is the furthest the conversation actually got.
deal_merging.rationale: Counting calls as deals double-counts prospects and understates close rate. The unit that matters commercially is the deal.
deal_merging.cash: Deal cash is taken from the closing call only, never summed across calls in the sequence.
deal_merging.adherence: Adherence stays scored per call. A discovery call and a follow-up call are judged against different parts of the script, so averaging them would hide which part failed.

junk_filter.detail: Transcripts below 2 KB are failed or aborted recordings — connection drops, no-shows, empty rooms. Observed examples in the corpus run from 96 bytes to roughly 1.2 KB.
junk_filter.reporting: Excluded files are counted and reported, never silently dropped. A rising junk count is itself a signal about recording setup.

close_rule.detail: A verbal agreement to move forward plus a payment link sent counts as CLOSED, even where the transcript ends before payment confirms.
close_rule.known_bias: Overstates close rate against any deal that agreed and then never paid. Joining a payments export would quantify the gap.
close_rule.cash_treatment: Where a payment plan was agreed, cash is recorded as contract value with the instalment terms retained separately, so cash-collected and contract-value can be reported apart.
